deep.reconstruction:
This page has no calculations. It is a philosophical draft, the continuation of Riemann's 'Antinomien' sketch begun on the previous page (31r), with headings I–IV, Thesis = finitude/representability and Antithesis = infinity/continuity.

Top of the page, the antinomy pair for the world as a whole:
- Thesis (left): 'Einfache [or Endliche] Elemente' (the word 'Stoff' is struck out), and 'eine in zeitlicher Entwicklung begriffene Gotteswelt', i.e. a divine world in temporal development.
- Antithesis (right): 'Stetiges' and 'Zeitloses Reich (…)'. The timeless realm is glossed as what contributes the purposive (Zweckmässiges) and the ethically and aesthetically valuable.

Centre heading: 'Allgemeines Verhältniss der Begriffssysteme der Thesis und Antithesis', i.e. the general relation between the conceptual systems of thesis and antithesis.

Riemann then answers this with the mathematical model of the limit method (Grenzmethode). He says it is the method Newton used to found the calculus, and that since the start of the 19th century the best mathematicians have recognised it as the only one giving secure results. His description, restated in modern terms (the formalisation is mine):
- Take a continuous transition from one value, place, or 'mode of determination of a concept', say a to b.
- First replace it by a transition through finitely many intermediate stages, a = x_0 < x_1 < … < x_n = b.
- Then let n grow so that all successive gaps shrink to zero: max_i |x_i − x_{i−1}| → 0.

The intended application is philosophical. The continuum and the infinite (antithesis) are to be grasped as limits of the finite and representable (thesis), so the two conceptual systems are linked rather than contradictory. This is a 'limit' resolution of a Kantian antinomy, and it ties in with the next page's excerpt (Saint-Venant/Cauchy on discrete molecules versus continuity).

The last lines return to the timeless realm, which 'inserts/adds' (hineinfügt/hinzufügt) the purposive and the ethically and aesthetically valuable into the world.

No derivation is present. The only mathematical content is the verbal definition of passing to the limit over partitions with mesh tending to zero.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no computation.

Historical point: crediting Newton with the 'Grenzmethode' (prime and ultimate ratios) is defensible. The rigorous limit-based foundation, though, is really due to Cauchy (1821) and Bolzano, which is what 'seit Anfang dieses Jahrhunderts' refers to.
The description requires only that successive gaps go to zero. This is the correct condition (mesh → 0), consistent with Riemann's own 1854 definition of the integral.

results.what: Verbal definition of the limit method: approximate a continuous transition by finitely many intermediate stages, then refine so that all successive gaps tend to zero.
results.modern_name: Limit of partitions with mesh tending to zero (the Cauchy/Riemann limit concept)
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (prime and ultimate ratios, 1687); rigorous form Cauchy 1821, Bolzano

results.what: Using the limit method as a model for reconciling the finite/representable (thesis) with the continuous/infinite (antithesis) in the antinomies.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published in the Nachlass section of the Gesammelte Werke, Weber/Dedekind, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts')

deep.surprise_reason: This is a philosophical draft. As far as I know, essentially this text, including the Grenzmethode passage, was printed in the 'Antinomien' section of Riemann's collected works. Its mathematical content is the standard limit concept.

checkable.asserts: Example of the limit method: a sum over n equal subintervals (mesh 1/n → 0) converges to the integral of x**2 over [0,1], which is 1/3. The expression should equal 0.
The mesh of the uniform partition tends to 0, as the method requires.

transcription_corrections: The top-left heading reads 'Thesis' (written small), and the right heading reads 'Antithesis'. Both are correct.
The first thesis line, 'Einfache[?] Elemente', might read 'Endliche Elemente'. The handwriting is ambiguous. The struck word after it is probably 'Stoff'.
On the right, 'Stetiges' is written as a separate small heading above the struck 'Zeitloses'.
The parenthesis after 'Zeitloses Reich' is in a later hand at the far right, possibly '(Gesetze und Lauterkeiten)'. The 'Geister' reading is uncertain.
The far-right bracketed note probably reads 'Zwecke u. ästhetische Werthe … sittlich und ästhetisch Werthvolles'. It duplicates the line beside it.
In the final paragraph, 'hineinfügt' may be 'hinzufügt'. The reading 'Ausgehen' is uncertain; 'das zu diesem' is followed by a struck 'welches das'.
